name: Helium Harvest

stars.name: Dim Hearth
stars.notes: Cool, stable star at the boundary of K and M classification. Low luminosity keeps the system cold, but long-term stability has allowed gas giant atmospheres to remain undisturbed for billions of years.

planets.name: Cinder
planets.notes: Airless inner rock with a cratered surface. No significant mineral deposits; serves only as a gravitational anchor for inner system navigation.

planets.name: Tank Farm
planets.notes: Primary helium-3 harvesting target. Its atmosphere is exceptionally rich in helium-3 due to billions of years of stellar wind implantation and atmospheric retention.

planets.name: Reserve
planets.notes: Secondary gas giant with lower helium-3 concentration but significant hydrogen reserves. Harvested for supplementary fuel production.

planets.name: Icecap
planets.notes: Frozen outer body with helium-rich frost deposits on its surface--a phenomenon unique to this system's unusual atmospheric chemistry.

anomalies.name: The Whisper Layer
anomalies.notes: Skimmer crews report audible harmonic tones transmitted through hull vibrations when operating in a specific atmospheric layer of Tank Farm. The phenomenon is consistent and reproducible but physically unexplained.

asteroid_belts.name: Gravel Line
asteroid_belts.notes: Thin belt of rocky and icy debris. Minimal commercial value but occasionally harvested for water ice to supply station operations.

stations.name: Harvest Platform One
stations.notes: Automated helium-3 extraction and compression facility. Small crew manages the skimmer drone fleet that operates continuously in Tank Farm's atmosphere.

stations.name: Reserve Tap
stations.notes: Secondary extraction station with minimal crew. Operates on demand when helium-3 prices justify harvesting Reserve's lower-concentration atmosphere.

faction_control.notes: Sister operation to Gas Tap Hollow, operated by the same Collective. Helium Harvest's specialized helium-3 output complements the hydrogen-focused operations elsewhere in the Collective's portfolio.

history: Cataloged in 2467 as part of the Nimbus Fuel Collective's systematic survey of gas giant systems in the outer Nimbus Verge.
Tank Farm's exceptional helium-3 concentration was confirmed in 2470, prompting deployment of extraction infrastructure that reached operational status by 2474.

The Whisper Layer was first reported in 2481 by skimmer pilot Olen Dray, who described it as 'the planet humming a tune.' Subsequent investigations confirmed the phenomenon but failed to identify its cause.
description: Helium Harvest exists for a single, extraordinarily valuable resource: helium-3. Four worlds orbit the dim orange-red star Dim Hearth, but only Tank Farm matters commercially. Billions of years of stellar wind bombardment and atmospheric retention have concentrated helium-3 in Tank Farm's upper atmosphere at levels ten times the galactic average, making it one of the most efficient extraction sites known. The system is quiet, cold, and purposeful--a fuel depot at the edge of settled space.

The Nimbus Fuel Collective operates Helium Harvest with characteristic efficiency. Harvest Platform One coordinates fleets of skimmer drones that dip into Tank Farm's atmosphere, compress the harvested gases, and package helium-3 into fuel cells that power fusion reactors across the sector. The operation is small-scale by mining standards--fewer than 350 permanent personnel across both stations--but the value per unit of output is staggering. A single fuel cell from Helium Harvest is worth more than a bulk freighter of iron ore, making the system's modest traffic deceptively lucrative.

The Whisper Layer in Tank Farm's atmosphere has become the system's unofficial calling card. Every skimmer pilot who has operated in the affected atmospheric band reports the same experience: harmonic tones, clearly audible through hull vibrations, that shift in pitch and pattern without correlating to any known atmospheric phenomenon. The Collective has funded three separate studies, none conclusive. Some pilots find it unsettling; others consider it a good luck charm, timing their harvesting runs to coincide with the tones. Icecap's surface helium frost deposits, unique in known space, suggest the system's unusual atmospheric chemistry may extend beyond Tank Farm--a geological curiosity that researchers have petitioned to study, so far without success.
